answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the canyon index resolves every citation against the jade checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the forge audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 64 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 64 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 10 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
